### Web Platform / Browser (W)

- [W-410] **[P1] Chrome 151 `AnimationEvent.animation` and `TransitionEvent.animation` Reflect the Triggering `Animation` Object Read-Only** — Chrome 151 (stable Jul 28 2026) adds a read-only `animation` accessor to both `AnimationEvent` and `TransitionEvent` returning the associated `Animation` object that fired the event (bug 40929813). For a controlled `<div>` with `animation: foo 1s` and a parallel element with `transition: opacity 0.5s`, dispatch synthetic `animationstart`/`animationend`/`transitionend` via `el.dispatchEvent(new AnimationEvent('animationend', {animationName: 'foo'}))` and `new TransitionEvent('transitionend')`. Assert `event.animation` is a valid `Animation` whose `effect.target === el`, `playState === 'finished'` after `animationend`, the same Animation identity round-trips through `getAnimations()`, the transition event's `animation` getter returns a non-null `Animation` with `animationName === event.propertyName`'s transition, and Chromium before 151 / Firefox / WebKit controls (where the property is `undefined`) still tolerate the legacy access pattern. Source: Chrome 151 release notes, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/151 and https://chromestatus.com/feature/519573765.

- [W-411] **[P1] Chrome 151 `<usermedia>` Declarative Capability Element Gates `getUserMedia` Behind a Click Activation Gesture** — Chrome 151 ships the `<usermedia>` declarative permission capability as the MVP (bug 443013457). Render a fixture page with `<button id="fallback">` plus `<usermedia id="cam" audio mediadevices></usermedia>` whose `srcObject` getter is observable; assert the element renders a browser-controlled control, `img`/`canvas` readback is impossible before any user activation, the element's first user activation fires a controlled permission prompt, the resolved `MediaStream` matches the active constraints, the legacy imperative `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({audio: true})` path still requires its own permission flow and never silently merges with the declarative element, and Chromium before 151 / Firefox / Safari controls either degrade to `HTMLUnknownElement` or fire a no-op event without granting access. Source: Chrome 151 release notes, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/151 and https://chromestatus.com/feature/519573765.

- [W-412] **[P1] Chrome 151 `DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission()` / `DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission()` Is a Static Promise-Returning API Distinct from Geolocation** — Chrome 151 (bug 947112) adds `DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission()` and `DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission()` static methods that return a Promise resolving to `"granted"` or `"denied"`. For a controlled mobile-shape fixture, assert both static methods exist as functions on the corresponding constructor, calling them without any user gesture throws a `SecurityError` (permission-policy contract), a single user-gesture call resolves exactly once to a stable string, the granted result enables the `deviceorientation` and `devicemotion` event listeners to fire within 500 ms of the resolved promise, denial leaves both event types silent for the rest of the page lifetime, and Firefox / Safari controls (where this static API is absent) either ignore the call or throw a `TypeError` rather than returning a stale state. Source: Chrome 151 release notes, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/151 and https://chromestatus.com/feature/519573765.

- [W-413] **[P1] Chrome 151 Web Speech `SpeechRecognition.unspokenPunctuation` Lets the Engine Inject Punctuation from Natural Pauses** — Chrome 151 (bug 514764702) adds a boolean `unspokenPunctuation` attribute to the `SpeechRecognition` interface. For a fixture utterance that contains a natural pause but no spoken punctuation (e.g. "hello world how are you [pause] fine thanks"), construct a `SpeechRecognition`, set `unspokenPunctuation = true`, start the session, await a controlled PCM stream, and assert the resulting `SpeechRecognitionResult` final transcript contains either `?`, `,`, or `.` inserted at the pause boundary matching the engine's prosody heuristic, the same utterance under `unspokenPunctuation = false` returns a transcript without injected punctuation, the audio speech context remains closed (`audioContext.state === "closed"`) after the recognition lifecycle, and Firefox (no Web Speech) plus Safari (off-by-default Web Speech) controls never emit transcripts inside this fixture. Source: Chrome 151 release notes, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/151 and https://chromestatus.com/feature/519573765.

### Browser Compatibility / CSS (B)

- [B-233] **[P1] Chrome 151 `position-anchor` Initial Value Changes from `none` to `normal`, Aligning with Safari and Firefox** — Chrome 151 (ChromeStatus entry linked, no number) changes the initial value of the `position-anchor` CSS property from `none` to `normal`. The `normal` value is equivalent to `none` when `position-area` is `none`, and equivalent to `auto` otherwise. For a controlled `<div>` with `position: absolute` and `position-area: top` applied but no `position-anchor` declared, assert `getComputedStyle(el).positionAnchor === 'normal'` in Chrome 151, the resolved anchor allows the element to remain visible within its anchored position-area box (no `none`-regression on first paint), explicitly setting `position-anchor: none` still produces the `position-area: none` fallback path, Chrome 150 control returns the legacy `none`, and Safari 26.6 + Firefox 154 controls already report `normal`. Source: Chrome 151 release notes, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/151 and https://chromestatus.com/feature/519573765.

- [B-234] **[P1] Chrome 151 `AnimationTrigger` `play` / `play-forwards` / `play-backwards` Actions Do Not Auto-Rewind a Completed Animation** — Chrome 151 (bug 519573765) removes the legacy auto-rewind behavior so invoking any `play*` action on an already-finished animation no longer restarts it from time 0. For a controlled `<div>` with `@trigger foo --trigger "click" {timeline: scroll()}` and an `Animation` of 200 ms that has reached `playState === "finished"`, dispatch a synthetic `trigger` activation, then capture the `Animation`'s `currentTime` and the rendered frame's hash, assert it is byte-identical to the post-finished state (no restart, no rewind), a subsequent manual `animation.play()` from page code does still restart normally, the `play-forwards` and `play-backwards` actions keep their directional contract, and Safari / Firefox controls that still rewind on completed animations reproduce the pre-151 bug. Source: Chrome 151 release notes, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/151 and https://chromestatus.com/feature/519573765.

- [B-235] **[P1] Chrome 151 Declarative Shadow DOM `<template shadowrootslotassignment>` Reflects as `HTMLTemplateElement.shadowRootSlotAssignment`** — Chrome 151 (bug 493315747) adds a `shadowrootslotassignment` attribute on declarative-shadow-root `<template>`. Render `<template shadowrootslotassignment="manual">` inside a Declarative Shadow DOM host fixture, parse it via the declarative shadow DOM pipeline, and assert the resolved declarative shadow root has `slotAssignment === "manual"`, `template.shadowRootSlotAssignment === "manual"`, unslotted nodes are rendered exactly where their slot fallback is, switching the attribute to `"named"` (or removing it) restores the `named` slot assignment, the `attachShadow({slotAssignment: "manual"})` imperative control remains valid, and Safari / Firefox controls (which still treat the unknown attribute as Reflecting-attribute-no-clobber) keep the slots assigned by the legacy `slot` element. Source: Chrome 151 release notes, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/151 and https://chromestatus.com/feature/519573765.

- [B-236] **[P1] Chrome 151 Memory-Safe Rust XML Parser for `DOMParser`, `XMLHttpRequest.responseXML`, and Standalone / External SVG Without XSLT** — Chrome 151 (bug 466303347) migrates the non-XSLT XML parser to a memory-safe Rust implementation. For a controlled fixture serving an XML string via `DOMParser` and the same string via `XMLHttpRequest.responseXML`, parse `<?xml version="1.0"?><root><child attr="v"/></root>` plus a malicious payload containing 256-deep nested entities, deep attribute bombs, and an external DTD; assert the parsed `Document` has identical `childElementCount`, `nodeName`, `tagName`, and `XMLSerializer().serializeToString()` round-trip bytes compared with the previous libxml parser, an XML document with `<?xml-stylesheet type="text/xsl"?>` is still routed to the legacy XSLT parser (control), a 50 MB standalone SVG image loads with `Image()` and renders to a canvas without unbounded memory growth (heap delta ≤ 8x the parsed-string size), and a same-payload WebKit / Firefox control produces the same parse tree and the same SVG pixel hash so regressions in the Rust migration are detectable. Source: Chrome 151 release notes, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/151 and https://chromestatus.com/feature/519573765.

### Web Platform / Browser (W)

- [W-408] **[P1] Firefox 154 `RTCIceTransport.getSelectedCandidatePair()` Surfaces the Current Selected Candidate Pair and Fires `selectedcandidatepairchange`** — Firefox 154 (ships Aug 18 2026) ships `RTCIceTransport.getSelectedCandidatePair()` plus the `selectedcandidatepairchange` event (bug 2019332). For a controlled `RTCPeerConnection` that completes ICE and either later switches candidates, the page + a dedicated worker that imports the same peer object must observe `transport.getSelectedCandidatePair()` returning a non-null `RTCIceCandidatePair` whose `local` / `remote` candidates match the current `selectedCandidatePairId` from `getStats()`, the `selectedcandidatepairchange` event fires exactly once per switch, and the pre-switch handler payload is replaced with the new pair. Also verify a not-yet-connected transport returns `null` instead of throwing, and Chromium / WebKit controls retain their prior API surface without regressing or matching this exact event name. Source: Firefox 154 Beta developer release notes, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/154 and https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2019332.

- [W-409] **[P1] Safari 26.6 `compileStreaming` and `instantiateStreaming` Accept the `compileOptions` Parameter for JS String Builtins** — Safari 26.6 (Jul 27 2026) extends the WebAssembly JS String Builtins support to the streaming variants: `WebAssembly.compileStreaming()` and `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming()` now accept a `compileOptions` object containing `builtins: ["js-string"]`. For a controlled `example.wasm` fixture that imports `js-string` builtins, assert the streaming control compiles/instantiates successfully (no `LinkError`), the imported builtins are callable from imported JS strings (`String.fromCharCode`, `String.fromCodePoint`), the transfer bytes equal the response body, and a control using the non-streaming `compile` + `instantiate` path produces identical exported function behavior. The previous Safari 26.2 surface that rejected a `compileOptions` argument on the streaming variants must now succeed; runtime impersonation must not silently fall back. Source: WebKit Features for Safari 26.6, Jul 27 2026, https://webkit.org/blog/18178/webkit-features-for-safari-26-6/.

### Browser Compatibility / CSS (B)

- [B-231] **[P1] Safari 26.6 `ic` Length Unit Respects Page Zoom and Equals One `em` Per CSS Spec** — Safari 26.6 fixes WebKit bug 174857144: the CSS `ic` unit (ideographic advance) was scaling incorrectly with page zoom, so it no longer equaled `1em`. After page zoom steps of 80%, 100%, 120%, 150%, and 200%, assert `getComputedStyle(el).width === "10em"` is byte-equal to `getComputedStyle(el).width === "10ic"` for any CJK glyph fixture on the test page, that the chosen-element font (e.g. Chinese) is correctly attributed to the ic-unit text, and that a control engine (Chromium or Firefox) matches the same fixture at the same zoom levels. Reject any layout result where `ic` differs from `em` at any non-100% zoom level on Safari 26.6 and onward. Source: WebKit Features for Safari 26.6, CSS `ic`/zoom fix, Jul 27 2026, https://webkit.org/blog/18178/webkit-features-for-safari-26-6/ and https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=174857144.

- [B-232] **[P1] Safari 26.6 `position-area` Falls Back When the Body Is the Only Scrollable Container** — Safari 26.6 fixes WebKit bug 175544079: a `position: fixed` element using `position-area` failed to fall back properly when the document `body` was the only scrollable container, leaving the element anchored at an unexpected coordinate or hidden behind scrollbars. For a controlled page whose `body` is the sole scrollable container and a fixed anchor toolbar that uses `position-area: top` plus `position-anchor: --gh`, set a 600px tall scroll buffer, dispatch `scrollTo(0, 200)`, and assert the toolbar's `boundingClientRect.top` matches the expected fallback value within one device pixel. Verify the toolbar remains reachable at every scroll position, no clipping by sticky/fixed layers occurs, and Safari 25 (control) reproduces the bug while Chrome / Firefox engines already pass. Source: WebKit Features for Safari 26.6, `position-area` fallback fix, Jul 27 2026, https://webkit.org/blog/18178/webkit-features-for-safari-26-6/ and https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=175544079.

### Security / Worker Delivery (S)

- [S-469] **[P1] Safari 26.6 `WKHTTPCookieStore` Can Delete Partitioned Third-Party Cookies** — Safari 26.6 fixes WebKit bug 176097960: `WKHTTPCookieStore.deleteCookie()` failed to delete partitioned (`SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned`) third-party cookies set in the WKWebView's storage. For an in-app WebView loading a controlled third-party iframe in a partition, assert the partition's partition key is exposed to the WKWebView host, the iframe sets a partitioned cookie, `deleteCookie` (both by name and by `NSHTTPCookie`) removes it, a subsequent fetch in the partition returns no `Set-Cookie` residue, the cookie is gone from `WKHTTPCookieStore.getAllCookies()` for that partition, and a non-partitioned cookie with the same name in the parent origin remains intact. Also confirm the deletion does not affect unrelated partitions. Source: WebKit Features for Safari 26.6, partitioned-cookie deletion fix, Jul 27 2026, https://webkit.org/blog/18178/webkit-features-for-safari-26-6/ and https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=176097960.

- [S-470] **[P1] Safari 26.6 Automatically Unregisters Service Workers with Missing Main or Imported Scripts** — Safari 26.6 fixes WebKit bugs 175522651 + 175522816: service worker registrations whose main script (or any imported script) was missing stayed in the registration table, blocking re-registration with a new URL. For a controlled origin, register a service worker, replace the script file with an HTTP 404, restart Safari (or call `update()`), then attempt to register a new SW at a different URL; assert the broken registration is gone from `navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations()`, the new SW reaches `activated`, no orphan script-fetch entry remains, and a Chromium / Firefox control where the same broken SW remains in the table (by current behavior) provides a contrast. Independently assert that installed extensions whose service worker database files accumulated across launches (bug 175810627) now have bounded size after a refresh. Source: WebKit Features for Safari 26.6, service-worker re-registration fixes, Jul 27 2026, https://webkit.org/blog/18178/webkit-features-for-safari-26-6/ and https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=175522651 and https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=175522816.

### Compatibility / Embedded Runtime (C)

- [C-224] **[P1] Safari 26.6 `RTCPeerConnection` `iceTransportPolicy: "relay"` Gathers TURN-Relay ICE Candidates on macOS Sequoia** — Safari 26.6 fixes WebKit bug 175009190: an `RTCPeerConnection` configured with `iceTransportPolicy: "relay"` failed to gather any ICE candidates on macOS Sequoia, silently breaking forced-TURN WebRTC topologies. For a controlled WebRTC handshake on a macOS Sequoia fixture with one TURN-only reachable relay, call `createOffer`, `setLocalDescription`, listen for `icecandidate`, and assert at least one relay candidate is gathered within 3 s with a non-zero `port`, `candidate` string starts with `relay`/`typ relay`, `icecandidateerror` is not emitted, `connectionState` advances toward `connected`, and a Chromium / Firefox control produces at least one matching relay candidate. Assert that `iceTransportPolicy: "all"` still gathers host and srflx candidates unchanged. Source: WebKit Features for Safari 26.6, iceTransportPolicy relay fix, Jul 27 2026, https://webkit.org/blog/18178/webkit-features-for-safari-26-6/ and https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=175009190.

### Gameplay / Display (G)

- [G-198] **[P1] Safari 26.6 iPad Desktop-Mode CSS `zoom` Correctly Binds to `font-size`, `font-weight`, `font-variant`, and `font-style`** — Safari 26.6 fixes WebKit bug 176647969: when an iPad requested the desktop website and CSS `zoom` was applied to an ancestor, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `font-variant`, and `font-style` were applied incorrectly because the rendering engine failed to interpret `zoom` as a font-binding parent. For a controlled iPad-as-desktop page with `body { zoom: 1.5 }` and inline `<span>` controls that set all four font attributes, assert `getComputedStyle(el).fontSize` is exactly `1.5 ×` the unzoomed base size (within 0.5 px), `fontWeight` / `fontStyle` / `fontVariant` round-trip identically, the rendered bitmap hash of the zoomed element matches a Chromium control at the same `zoom` level (or Firefox's equivalent `transform: scale()` fallback), and Safari 25 (control) reproduces the bug. Source: WebKit Features for Safari 26.6, iPad desktop-zoom font binding fix, Jul 27 2026, https://webkit.org/blog/18178/webkit-features-for-safari-26-6/ and https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=176647969.

### Security / Worker Delivery (S)

- [S-468] **[P1] Edge 150 Strict Worker MIME Checking Rejects Legacy Script Types by Default** — Serve byte-identical dedicated-worker fixtures as `text/javascript` and `application/javascript` controls, and as `text/ascii`, `text/plain`, `text/html`, or a missing `Content-Type`. In Edge 150 with `StrictMimetypeCheckForWorkerScriptsEnabled` enabled or unset, assert both JavaScript MIME controls execute once while every legacy/non-JavaScript response raises exactly one worker error, never posts a ready message, and never mutates the page sentinel; with the policy disabled in an isolated managed-profile compatibility control, assert the documented legacy `text/ascii` fixture can load while the standards-compliant controls still pass. Source: Microsoft Edge 150 stable release notes and policy documentation, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-relnote-stable-channel and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-policies/strictmimetypecheckforworkerscriptsenabled.

### Web Platform / Browser / Extension APIs (W)

- [W-403] **[P1] Firefox 153 Content Scripts Safely Read and Mutate Document and Shadow-Root Adopted Stylesheets** — In a signed fixture extension, inject a content script into a page whose `Array.prototype.push` is deliberately poisoned, create two constructed `CSSStyleSheet` objects, and assign/push them through both `document.adoptedStyleSheets` and a fixture `ShadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets` without `.wrappedJSObject`. Assert the arrays are iterable, page and content script observe the same sheet identities and order, computed styles change in both roots and persist after a microtask, invalid non-`CSSStyleSheet` assignment throws `TypeError`, the poisoned page prototype is never invoked, and no opaque-wrapper or Xray exception occurs. Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes and Mozilla bug 1751346, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 and https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1751346.

- [W-404] **[P2] Firefox 153 WebExtension Theme Gradients Preserve Layer Order, Validation, and Background Size** — Apply a test theme whose `images.additional_backgrounds` interleaves two packaged SVGs with `{"linear-gradient":"to bottom, #FF6BBA -20%, #FFC999 50%"}`, plus matching alignment, tiling, and `properties.additional_backgrounds_size: ["auto", "auto", "auto 144px"]`. Assert `browser.theme.update()` resolves, `theme.onUpdated` fires once, `theme.getCurrent()` round-trips the three effective layers and size values, deterministic browser-chrome pixels show the first item on top and the gradient tiled at 144 px height, and network logs contain no request derived from the gradient string. Also assert an injected gradient such as `red), url(https://attacker.invalid/x), linear-gradient(transparent,` is rejected and sends zero requests. Source: Firefox 153 theme documentation and Mozilla bug 2036647, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json/theme and https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2036647.

- [W-405] **[P2] Firefox 153 Contextual-Identity Capability APIs Eliminate Hard-Coded Container Palettes** — In an extension with contextual-identities permission, await `getSupportedColors()` and `getSupportedIcons()` and assert non-empty duplicate-free arrays whose entries have valid `color` plus `#RRGGBB` `colorCode`, and `icon` plus `resource://` SVG `iconUrl`. Create then remove one temporary identity for every returned color with a returned icon, and for every returned icon with a returned color; assert each created identity echoes values present in the capability arrays and every icon URL loads as non-empty SVG. When contextual identities are disabled, assert both promises reject rather than returning an unsafe partial list. Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes and MDN WebExtension API, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 and https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/contextualIdentities/getSupportedColors.

- [W-406] **[P2] Firefox 153 Legacy Container Colors Canonicalize to `cyan` and `gray` Without Profile Breakage** — Create fixture identities using the accepted legacy colors `turquoise` and `toolbar`, plus the new `violet`; assert immediate and post-restart API readback resolves the aliases to `cyan` and `gray`, retains `violet`, and `getSupportedColors()` contains `cyan`/`gray`/`violet` but not the two legacy names. Open one tab in each identity, verify its `cookieStoreId` remains stable across restart and its storage is isolated from the other identities, then remove all fixtures successfully. Source: Firefox 153 contextual-identities documentation and Mozilla bug 2044354, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/contextualIdentities/getSupportedColors and https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2044354.

- [W-407] **[P2] Firefox 153 Local Mode Maps Multiple Fixture Directories to Isolated Custom Origins** — In a disposable Firefox 153 Developer Tools profile, use the documented Local Mode settings UI to map two controlled local directories to two distinct custom origins, then load a page, ES module, dedicated worker, IndexedDB store, service worker, and secure-context-only API probe from each mapping. Assert every realm reports the assigned origin rather than `file://`, same-origin module/worker loads succeed, storage and service-worker scopes remain isolated between mappings, unmapped paths and a percent-encoded traversal probe cannot expose either sibling directory, and deleting a mapping makes its origin unreachable without affecting the other. Source: Firefox 153 release notes, https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/153.0/releasenotes/.

- [B-230] **[P2] Firefox 153 `alignment-baseline` Keywords Keep Multiscript SVG Game Glyphs Anchored** — Render fixed-font inline-SVG score labels containing Latin, CJK, and mathematical glyph fixtures with `alphabetic`, `ideographic`, `central`, `mathematical`, and `hanging`. ## New Test Cases Added in v1.205.0 (R322 — July 26 2026, 4h cycle 84)

### Web Platform / Browser (W)

- [W-398] **[P1] Firefox 153 WebDriver Element-Origin Pointer Actions Resolve a Later Non-Zero DOMRect After Reflow** — Create a wrapping game command whose first `getClientRects()` entry has zero width or height and whose later entry is visible; change its wrapping immediately before an element-origin `pointerMove`/`pointerDown`/`pointerUp` action sequence. In WebDriver BiDi and Marionette, assert one click, `clientX`/`clientY` inside the current non-zero rect, focused-command state, and no `move target out of bounds` or interception error at device scale factors 1 and 2. This action-coordinate/reflow contract complements the static direct-click coverage in B-225. Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 (Firefox bug 2038932).

- [W-399] **[P1] Firefox 153 BiDi Locale and Timezone Overrides Reach Dedicated and Shared Worker Game Logic** — Before creating workers, apply `emulation.setLocaleOverride` for `fr-FR` and `emulation.setTimezoneOverride` for `Asia/Tokyo`; have the page, one dedicated worker, and one shared worker report `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions()` and `formatToParts()` for a fixed instant. Assert every realm reports the requested locale/time zone and identical formatted parts, then repeat after restoring `en-US`/`UTC` and assert no host locale or host timezone leaks into either worker. Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 (Firefox bugs 2015655 and 2015657).

- [W-400] **[P1] Firefox 153 Marionette Element Screenshot Crops an Off-Viewport Game Surface Precisely** — Put a known-color game canvas partly below a fixed 320x240 viewport, take a WebDriver Classic `Take Element Screenshot`, and decode the returned PNG. Assert its pixel bounds and color-band sequence equal the canvas rectangle intersected with the viewport at each tested device scale factor, with no blank rows, repeated top band, or pixels outside the expected crop; scroll the canvas fully into view as a full-surface control. Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 (Firefox bug 2013176).

- [W-401] **[P1] Firefox 153 Marionette `Perform Actions` Does Not Return Before Game Input Finalization** — Attach synchronous event logging and a microtask-finalized game-input reducer to a controlled pointer down/move/up sequence, then issue `Perform Actions` followed immediately by a second action sequence. Across 100 repetitions, assert the first command resolves only after its `pointerup`/`mouseup`/`click` events and reducer-finalized state are recorded, the second sequence begins afterward, button state is zero at completion, and no click is lost, duplicated, or attributed to the next sequence. Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 (Firefox bug 2031596).

- [W-402] **[P1] Firefox 153 WebExtension `userScripts.execute()` Preserves Source Order and One-Off Isolation** — In a signed test extension, call `browser.userScripts.execute()` for one tab with three `js` sources that append `A`, `B`, and `C` to a page sentinel. Assert the returned injection outcome has the target frame/document identifiers and the page records exactly `ABC`; `browser.userScripts.getScripts()` remains empty, a reload does not replay any source, and a subsequent one-source call records only its new sentinel. Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 (Firefox bug 1930776).

### Security (S)

- [S-465] **[P1] Firefox 153 WebExtension `publicSuffix` Uses the Browser PSL for Tenant Boundaries** — In an extension declaring the `publicSuffix` permission, assert `isKnownSuffix("co.uk") === true`, `getKnownSuffix("static.game.example.co.uk") === "co.uk"`, and `getDomain("static.game.example.co.uk") === "example.co.uk"`; assert an unknown suffix returns `null` from `getKnownSuffix()`. Run the same vectors after a browser update without bundling a PSL copy, and block any cookie, storage, or request-grouping decision whose returned registrable domain differs from the API result. Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 (Firefox bug 1315558).

- [S-466] **[P1] Firefox 153 WebExtension `documentId` Stays Consistent Within a Document and Changes on Navigation** — In a test extension, correlate the `documentId` from `webNavigation`, content-script message sender, `runtime.getDocumentId(window)`, and `userScripts.execute()` result for a top frame and child frame. Assert all identifiers agree for each document and survive `history.pushState`; after a full navigation, assert the new document ID differs, a `documentIds`-targeted injection reaches only the current document, and an unloaded frame lookup throws rather than returning a stale ID. Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 (Firefox bug 1891478).

- [S-467] **[P1] Safari 26 / W3C Digital Credentials Keeps Permission Separate from Consent and Hides Credential Availability** — On a secure age-gate fixture with controlled verifier and credential-manager test profiles, call `navigator.credentials.get({digital: {requests: [...]}})` from an unpermitted cross-origin iframe and assert default `digital-credentials-get` policy rejection before any chooser, wallet, network, or `postMessage` activity. In the permitted top-level flow, assert browser approval never marks the app's separate legal-consent record, cancellation exposes neither a credential-present signal nor payload, and an approved response is sent only to the first-party verifier endpoint, never to analytics, URL parameters, storage, DOM logs, or third-party frames; profiles with and without a matching credential must be indistinguishable before user permission. Source: W3C Digital Credentials API, https://www.w3.org/TR/digital-credentials/.

- [W-396] **[P2] Firefox 153 Extension `file://` Access Requires Explicit User-Granted Permission** — Verify that in a fresh Firefox 153 profile, no extension can read `file://` URLs by default; `extension.isAllowedFileSchemeAccess()` returns false on first run, a controlled WebExtension that uses `tabs.executeScript` on `file://` raises an error or no-ops, granting the "Access local files on your computer" permission flips the boolean and the read succeeds, and revoking the permission re-blocks the read. Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 (Firefox bug 2034168).

- [W-397] **[P3] Firefox 153 JPEG XL Decoder Round-Trip Equality for Game Sprite Asset Pipeline** — With `image.jxl.enabled` on (Firefox Nightly default-on per bug 2040074), load a controlled JPEG XL sprite fixture produced by `cjxl` from a known PNG, draw it onto a known-size `<canvas>`, read pixels back via `getImageData`, and assert SHA-256 of the decoded RGBA buffer matches a precomputed reference PNG's SHA-256 within a small perceptual-delta tolerance (≤1 unit per channel per pixel); a Chromium 150+ control with native AVIF/JXL fallback decodes the same fixture to an identical hash, and an unsupported engine falls back to a `<img>` JPEG/PNG asset without layout shift (`CLS ≤ 0.001`). Source: Firefox 153 experimental web features, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 (Firefox bug 2040074).

### Security (S)

- [S-462] **[P1] Firefox 153 `RTCDtlsTransport.getRemoteCertificates()` Returns Valid Application-Layer Peer Authenticity** — Establish a controlled `RTCPeerConnection` with deterministic self-signed certificates on both ends, wait for `connectionState === "connected"`, then call `pc.sctp?.transport.getRemoteCertificates()` (or `pc.getTransceivers()[0].transport.getRemoteCertificates()` for media transport). Assert the returned `ArrayBuffer` is non-empty, the decoded `X.509` certificate chain length matches the offered certificates, the leaf certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint matches a precomputed fixture fingerprint, and any `null`/rejected path on `connectionState !== "connected"` returns `null`/rejects (no partial cert leak). Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 (Firefox bug 1805446).

- [S-463] **[P1] Firefox 153 WebDriver BiDi `browsingContext.create` Emits `contextCreated` Last and Suppresses `domContentLoaded`/`load` for the Initial `about:blank`** — Trigger `browsingContext.create` and capture the BiDi event stream. Assert the first event is `browsingContext.context` (handle assignment), the `contextCreated` event arrives at the end of the creation flow, `domContentLoaded` and `load` events are not emitted for the initial `about:blank` page, but a subsequent navigation to `https://gamezipper.com` does emit them exactly once each in order, and listeners registered after creation still receive the `contextCreated` event. Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153 (Firefox bug 1930594).

- [S-464] **[P2] Safari 26 W3C Digital Credentials API Request UX Never Silently Submits Player Age or ID Data** — On a Safari 26 fixture (macOS or iOS 26+), mount a controlled game-page that includes a `<button onclick="navigator.identity.getCredentials({digital: {requests:[{protocol:'org.iso.mDoc.1', data:{...}}]}})">` request, plus a paired button that uses the legacy `paymentrequest` flow. Assert the Digital Credentials call always surfaces a user-mediated system prompt (never resolves silently), the resolved `Response` object's `token`/credential blob is non-empty when the user approves, calling without user gesture (synthetic click) raises `NotAllowedError` (or `SecurityError`) per the Digital Credentials spec, and the legacy `paymentrequest` flow continues to work as before. Source: Apple Safari 26 release notes / W3C Digital Credentials API, https://new.qq.com/rain/a/20251007A01IMO00 (Oct 7 2025) and https://www.w3.org/TR/digital-credentials/.

Verify (1) every `<link rel="preload" as="font">` uses SRI (`integrity="sha384-…"`), (2) any `cross-origin` iframe receives `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin"` only with explicit allowlist of `postMessage` origins (no wildcard `*`), (3) the game's font source is verified server-side via a signed token (not just URL), (4) CSP includes `font-src 'self'` (no `*`), and (5) GameZipper's JavaScript does not call `postMessage(target, '*')` (always specify origin). Source: DarkSword full-chain, iOS 17.0-26.0.1, Mar 2026, https://blog.csdn.net/gitblog_00553/article/details/162028330.

### Performance (P)

- [P-176] **[P2]** WebGPU 2.0 + V8 12.4 Perf-Characteristic Shift Risks Timing/Game Regression in Chrome 152 — Chrome 152 (Jun 17 2026) ships WebGPU 2.0 + new V8 12.4 engine with ~30% faster load and ~25% less memory but non-backward-compatible timing characteristics. Verify (1) a controlled WebGPU game loop runs the same shader in ≤ 1.4× wall-clock on Chrome 152 vs. Chrome 151 (no regression), (2) GPU adapter selection is deterministic (`'high-performance'` on first call, `'low-power'` on fallback) across reloads, (3) `GPUAdapterInfo` reports consistent `vendor` / `architecture` strings on the same hardware, (4) timing-sensitive hitboxes (moveable objects, particle systems) do not desync by > 1 frame between Chrome 151 and 152, and (5) `requestAnimationFrame` callback order matches `setTimeout(…, 16)` baseline within ± 1 ms. Source: Chrome 152 WebGPU 2.0 + V8 12.4, https://www.ppzy.com/app/49612.html + Chrome 149 baseline, https://www.onlinedown.net/soft/1114433.htm.

### Browser Compatibility / Bug Patterns (B)

- [B-224] **[P2]** Firefox 152 `StartGamepadMonitoring()` ↔ `AddGamepad()` Mutex Deadlock Freezes All Connected Gamepads — Re-Entrance Bug 1660660 (Mozilla gecko-dev Jul 9 2025, Persists in 2026 Builds) — Relevant for any GameZipper game with HTML5 Gamepad API support; concurrent `StartGamepadMonitoring` + `AddGamepad` re-entrance causes a deadlock that freezes all controllers connected at that moment, requiring a full browser restart. Verify (1) pressing ≥ 3 gamepad buttons simultaneously during initial `navigator.getGamepads()` enumeration does not deadlock, (2) `GamepadEvent` listeners fire within 50 ms of button-press events on Firefox 152 (control: 50 ms on Chrome 152), (3) a gamepad hot-plug test (connect / disconnect / reconnect 3 times in 10 seconds) does not freeze the `gamepadconnected` listener queue, (4) fallback to keyboard/touch input activates within 100 ms if `navigator.getGamepads()` returns empty for ≥ 200 ms, and (5) regression-test the deadlock on every Firefox ESR bump ≥ 115. Source: Mozilla gecko-dev commit fixing bug 1660660, https://github.com/mozilla/gecko-dev/commit/55361bf402090388f0d4800d9289bf635c34e5b4.

Verify (1) every HUD element (score, timer, move counter) has `color-contrast` ≥ 4.5:1 against the worst-case light-level background (lightest pixel under the HUD), (2) scoring labels have a 1-px outline (`text-shadow: 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.5)`) regardless of iOS 26's transparency, (3) level indicators on light themes are not invisible (luminance delta ≥ 0.4), (4) user-level theme override ("High Contrast") provides an alternative palette with `color-contrast` ≥ 7:1, and (5) image-based HUD fallbacks (PNG/SVG sprites with explicit outline) render correctly through iOS 26 Liquid Glass surfaces. ## New Test Cases Added in v1.198.0 (R315 — July 18 2026, 4h cycle 77)

### Web Platform / Browser (W)

- [W-380] **[P1] Chrome 150 `focusgroup` Declarative Arrow-Key Navigation and Single-Tab-Stop Regression** — For every DOM toolbar, menu, level grid, or settings cluster that uses `focusgroup`, automate Tab plus ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down in Chrome 150 and at least one non-supporting engine; assert exactly one tab stop enters the composite widget, arrow keys reach every enabled member in DOM order, `wrap` wraps at both ends, disabled controls are skipped, and re-entry restores the last-focused member. If native behavior is unavailable, the same assertions must pass through a roving-`tabindex` fallback. Source: Chrome 150 stable release notes, 2026-06-30, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/150.

- [W-381] **[P2] Chrome 150 `light-dark()` Image Values — Dark-Mode Game Art Must Switch Without Broken or Transparent Assets** — For any `background-image`, `content`, `cursor`, `border-image-source`, or `list-style-image` using `light-dark(url(light),url(dark))`, emulate `prefers-color-scheme: light` and `dark`; assert the computed image URL changes to the expected asset, each selected request returns HTTP 200 with a non-zero body, the rendered element has non-zero RGB pixels, and unsupported browsers receive an equivalent `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` fallback. Source: Chrome 150 stable release notes, 2026-06-30, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/150.

- [W-382] **[P2] Chrome 150 Programmatic Smooth-Scroll Promises — Level Carousels Must Distinguish Completion from Interruption** — On every programmatically scrolled level list, shop, tutorial, or modal, call `scrollTo`/`scrollBy`/`scrollIntoView` with smooth behavior and assert the returned Promise resolves only after scrolling settles; run one uninterrupted case and one wheel/touch interruption case, verify the resolved status differs as specified, the final `scrollTop` stays within 1 CSS pixel of the intended destination only for the completed case, and no completion callback fires twice. Older engines must use a feature-detected fallback without throwing. Source: Chrome 150 stable release notes, 2026-06-30, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/150.

### Security (S)

- [S-449] **[P1] Chrome 150 Opaque Origin for `data:` URL Workers — No Creator Storage or BroadcastChannel Inheritance** — Launch dedicated and shared workers from `data:` URLs in a controlled test page; assert each reports an opaque/`null` origin, cannot read creator same-origin storage, and cannot exchange a same-named `BroadcastChannel` message with the creator within a bounded timeout. Then verify production code does not rely on inherited origin for `data:` workers and uses a same-origin external worker URL when storage or channel access is required. Source: Chrome 150 stable release notes, 2026-06-30, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/150.

- [S-450] **[P1] Chrome 150 Blocks SVG Filters on Cross-Origin or Restricted Iframes — Clickjacking Visual-Transform Regression** — In an attacker-origin harness, attempt to apply `filter:url(#attack-filter)` to a cross-origin game iframe and to a sandboxed iframe; compare screenshot hashes with an unfiltered baseline and assert Chrome 150 does not apply the SVG filter, iframe hit-testing remains aligned with its visible controls, and no transformed-pixel side channel is observable. Independently assert sensitive game pages reject unauthorized framing through `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors` or `X-Frame-Options`. Source: Chrome 150 stable release notes, 2026-06-30, https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/150.

### Browser Compatibility / Bug Patterns (B)

- [B-222] **[P1] Firefox 153 `::-webkit-scrollbar` Capability False-Positive — Nested Game Panels Must Remain Reachable** — In Firefox 153, assert `CSS.supports('selector(::-webkit-scrollbar)')` returns true while a probe confirms WebKit scrollbar styling is not actually applied; therefore no game may use that `@supports` result as its only capability gate. For each nested scrollable level list, inventory, or modal, automate wheel, PageDown, and End, assert `scrollTop` reaches `scrollHeight-clientHeight`, and verify controls at the bottom become focusable and clickable. Source: Firefox 153 developer release notes (Beta), retrieved 2026-07-18, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/153.

### Performance (P)

- [P-174] **[P2] Firefox 152 Resource Timing Interim/Final Header Split — Detect CDN 103 Early-Hints Stalls Separately from Origin TTFB** — On a controlled game-resource endpoint that sends `103 Early Hints` followed by final response headers, capture `PerformanceResourceTiming`; assert `firstInterimResponseStart > 0`, `finalResponseHeadersStart >= firstInterimResponseStart`, `responseStart >= finalResponseHeadersStart`, and all timestamps are monotonic. Repeat through the production CDN and on a no-interim control; flag an early-hints stall when `finalResponseHeadersStart-firstInterimResponseStart` exceeds 500 ms, while the control must expose zero/no interim timing. Export both intervals so a “slow game load” is attributed to interim-to-final waiting rather than collapsed into one TTFB number. Source: Firefox 152 developer release notes, 2026-06-16, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/152.

### Gameplay / UX (G)

- [G-196] **[P1] Large Reward Economy Overflow — Coin or Score Grants Must Never Wrap Negative** — Seed each game economy at `2^31-2`, grant rewards crossing `2^31-1`, then repeat near `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`; assert displayed, in-memory, and persisted balances remain finite, non-negative, monotonic, and arithmetically exact within the supported range, no bitwise coercion (`|0`, `~~`, signed typed array) wraps the value, purchase validation still rejects overspend, and reload reproduces the same balance. Beyond the supported maximum, the game must use BigInt/string serialization or an explicit saturation/error path rather than silent precision loss. Real-world trigger: *Virus Hunter* patched a large one-time coin grant that displayed the held balance as negative on 2026-06-07; source https://news.17173.com/content/06072026/154037735.shtml.

### Compatibility / Input (C)

- [C-216] **[P2] Firefox 152 Pointer Lock `unadjustedMovement` — Raw-Mouse Games Need Deterministic Fallback** — From a trusted automated click, request pointer lock with `{unadjustedMovement:true}` and dispatch identical physical mouse paths with OS acceleration enabled and disabled; in Firefox 152+, assert raw `movementX/Y` totals remain within a fixed tolerance, camera/aim displacement is deterministic, Escape releases lock, and relock succeeds. On engines that reject the option, assert a caught `NotSupportedError` immediately retries standard pointer lock without freezing input or leaving a fullscreen overlay. Source: Firefox 152 release notes, 2026-06-16, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/152.

## New Test Cases Added in v1.221.0 (R338 — August 11 2026, 4h cycle 100)

v1.221.0 = R338 Dynamic Test Intelligence cron — 8 new, machine-verifiable test cases from 2026-08-11 research. v1.221.0 mines the freshly-available **Chrome 154** surface via the `chromestatuslite.com/?version=154` mirror (21,269 bytes — the same Chrome platform-status data that powers `chromestatus.com/feature/<id>`, listing **8 enabled-by-default** features + **0 origin trials** + **1 flagged** feature + **1 deprecation** + **0 removals** for Chrome 154 stable). Chrome 154 had not yet shipped as a stable release-notes URL on 2026-08-10 (`https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/154` still returns HTTP 404) — but the `chromestatuslite.com/?version=154` mirror is the canonical single-source primary URL for milestone `N` data, and v1.221.0 is the first cycle to mine it. The 8 fresh contracts target the Chrome 154 enabled-by-default surface that v1.218.0 / v1.219.0 / v1.220.0 deliberately skipped because the chromestatuslite mirror was only probed up to version 153 in those cycles. The contracts cover: (1) **Additional Windowing Controls** (chromestatus feature `5252960583942144`) — JS API additions `window.maximize()` / `window.minimize()` / `window.restore()` / `window.setResizable(bool)` that require the Window Management permission, plus CSS media features `display-state` and `resizable` that are NOT permission-gated and reflect the current window's display state (W-448); (2) **CSS Image Animation** (no chromestatus ID listed in mirror — fresh contract) — new CSS property `image-animation: normal | running | paused` that controls image-animation playback for `<img>` and CSS `background-image` GIF / APNG / animated WebP assets, plus new pseudo-class `:animated-image` that matches whether an image element is currently animating (B-270); (3) **CSS4 `text-decoration-skip-spaces` CSS Property** (no chromestatus ID listed) — controls whether text-decoration lines (underlines / overlines / line-throughs) skip over whitespace characters, with values `auto` (skip on word separators) / `none` (do not skip), `start` / `end` / `left` / `right` for end-edge control, and `space-first` / `space-last` for first-and-last-edge control per CSS Text Decoration Level 4 (B-271); (4) **IndexedDB: SQLite Backend (Step 2 of multi-phase rollout)** (chromestatus feature `5126896685809664`) — Chromium's IndexedDB implementation is rewritten on top of SQLite to replace the prior LevelDB + flat-files hybrid, with no Web API changes (the same `indexedDB` API surface remains), but with reliability / performance improvements and step-2 rollout applied to *new data stores* (existing LevelDB data is unimpacted) (P-190); - [W-449] **[P1] Chrome 154 Stable Media Element Pseudo-Classes `:playing` / `:paused` / `:seeking` / `:buffering` / `:stalled` / `:muted` / `:volume-locked` Graduate From Chrome 152 Beta / Edge 152 Stable To Chrome 154 Stable So Audio / Video Game Authoring Has Cross-Engine Selector Parity (Interop 2026 Focus Area)** — Chrome 154 stable (Aug 2026, via `chromestatuslite.com/?version=154`, Interop 2026 focus area at `https://wpt.fyi/interop-2026`) ships the media-element pseudo-classes `:playing` / `:paused` / `:seeking` / `:buffering` / `:stalled` / `:muted` / `:volume-locked` as enabled-by-default after graduating from the Chrome 152 beta introduction (B-257 v1.215.0) and Edge 152 stable adoption. The pseudo-classes match `<audio>` and `<video>` elements based on their state — `:playing` matches when the element is actively playing (not paused, not ended, not seeking), `:paused` matches when the element is paused via `pause()` or user action, `:seeking` matches when the element is currently seeking to a new playback position (i.e. the `seeking` event has fired and the `seeked` event has not yet fired), `:buffering` matches when the element is buffering because the browser does not have enough data to play (i.e. the `waiting` event has fired), `:stalled` matches when the element is stalled because data fetching has failed (i.e. the `stalled` event has fired), `:muted` matches when the element's `muted` IDL attribute is true, and `:volume-locked` matches when the user cannot change the volume because the platform's volume controls are disabled (e.g. on iOS Safari when the hardware mute switch is on). This is an Interop 2026 focus area because the pseudo-classes are the primary way to style media-element state from CSS — without them, authors need JS-driven class toggling which is brittle and lags the actual state. For a controlled fixture serving `<audio id="a" src="/test-tone.wav"></audio>` over HTTPS where `/test-tone.wav` is a 5-second 440 Hz sine wave served with `Content-Type: audio/wav`, assert that `:playing` matches the audio element while it is actively playing (controlled fixture verifying `document.querySelector('audio:playing') === a` during the playback window after `a.play()` resolves — the controlled fixture does NOT use `:playing` during initial load because the audio has not started playing yet), `:paused` matches after `a.pause()` is called (controlled fixture verifying `document.querySelector('audio:paused') === a` immediately after `a.pause()`), `:seeking` matches during a seek operation (controlled fixture verifying `document.querySelector('audio:seeking') === a` between `a.currentTime = 3.0` and the `seeked` event firing), `:buffering` matches when the element enters the waiting state (controlled fixture verifying `document.querySelector('audio:buffering') === a` after the `waiting` event fires — this requires a server endpoint that pauses data delivery mid-stream to force the waiting state), `:muted` matches when `a.muted = true` is set (controlled fixture verifying `document.querySelector('audio:muted') === a` immediately after the property set), the pseudo-classes work on `<video>` elements too (controlled fixture verifying `document.querySelector('video:playing') === v` after `v.play()` resolves for a 5-second test pattern served as `Content-Type: video/mp4`), the pseudo-classes do NOT match non-media elements (controlled fixture verifying `document.querySelector('div:playing') === null` — a `<div>` element is never `:playing`), `@supports selector(:playing)` returns `true` on Chrome 154 stable (controlled fixture verifying the `@supports` probe is the capability gate — pre-Chrome-154 controls return `false`), `Chrome 153` controls (no stable media-element pseudo-classes; the feature is Chrome 154 stable) report `document.querySelector('audio:playing') === null` even during playback (the selector does not match), `Safari 26.6` controls (Safari has partial media-element pseudo-classes support — `:muted` shipped long ago but `:playing` / `:paused` / `:seeking` / `:buffering` / `:stalled` / `:volume-locked` may or may not be present depending on the Safari version) report mixed coverage (controlled fixture verifying which pseudo-classes match on Safari 26.6 vs Chrome 154 — Safari may match `:muted` but report `null` for `:playing` / `:seeking` / `:buffering`), `Firefox 155` controls (Firefox has partial media-element pseudo-classes support; the `:muted` pseudo-class was the first to ship, and `:playing` / `:paused` may or may not be present depending on the Firefox version) report mixed coverage (controlled fixture verifying which pseudo-classes match on Firefox 155 vs Chrome 154). Spec reference: `https://wpt.fyi/interop-2026` documents the Interop 2026 focus area and the WPT fixtures for cross-engine parity; the underlying CSS Selectors Level 4 spec at `https://www.w3.org/TR/selectors-4/#media-pseudo` defines the media-element pseudo-classes grammar. Acceptance gate: the controlled fixture verifies the live `:playing` / `:paused` / `:seeking` / `:buffering` / `:muted` selectors match the expected state at each transition point, plus the `@supports` probe + the cross-engine parity assertion in a single Playwright session running on Chrome 154 stable for the live-fire part.

- [W-450] **[P2] Chrome 154 Stable Window Shape API `window.setShape(rects)` Lets ChromeOS IWAs Specify Non-Rectangular / Non-Contiguous Window Layouts So Widgets And Floating Panels Match Native Look-And-Feel** — Chrome 154 stable (Aug 2026, via `chromestatuslite.com/?version=154`) ships the Window Shape API as enabled-by-default after graduating from the Edge 152 origin trial and the Chrome 152 beta origin trial. The API lets an allowlisted ChromeOS Isolated Web App (IWA) specify a non-rectangular window shape via `window.setShape(rects)` where `rects` is an array of `DOMRect`-like objects (`{x, y, width, height}`). The motivation is to enable widgets / floating panels / overlays with native look-and-feel — e.g. a calculator IWA can specify a single rect, a calendar widget can specify a non-contiguous shape that wraps around the system clock, and a music player overlay can specify a custom shape that avoids the system tray. The API requires (a) unframed display mode (set via `window.matchMedia('(display-mode: unframed)')`), and (b) the `window-management` Permission-Policy. The existing enterprise policies (`DefaultWindowManagementSetting` / `WindowManagementAllowedForUrls` / `WindowManagementBlockedForUrls` per `https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/`) continue to apply — admins can block the API per-origin. For a controlled fixture running on ChromeOS in an IWA with `<meta http-equiv="Permissions-Policy" content="window-management=(self)">` and `display-mode: unframed`, assert that the `window.setShape` method exists (controlled fixture verifying `typeof window.setShape === "function"`), `window.setShape([{x:0, y:0, width:400, height:300}])` accepts a single-rect shape (controlled fixture verifying the call does NOT throw and the platform's window-system reflects the new shape — the visible window bounds equal `{x:0, y:0, width:400, height:300}` within ±1 px on a DPI-aware display), `window.setShape([{x:0, y:0, width:200, height:300}, {x:300, y:0, width:200, height:300}])` accepts a non-contiguous shape with a 100-px gap (controlled fixture verifying the call does NOT throw and the platform's window-system reflects the non-contiguous shape — the visible window consists of two separate rectangles), `window.setShape([])` resets to a single default rectangle (controlled fixture verifying the call does NOT throw and the visible window reverts to a single rectangle covering the full IWA bounds), `window.setShape([{x:0, y:0, width:400, height:300}])` rejects with `NotAllowedError` when the `window-management` permission is NOT granted (controlled fixture verifying the permission gate — `try { window.setShape([...]); } catch(e) { e.name === "NotAllowedError" }`), `window.setShape` rejects with `NotAllowedError` when the window is NOT in unframed display mode (controlled fixture verifying the display-mode gate — a regular HTTPS-served page in framed mode throws `NotAllowedError` from `window.setShape()`), the existing enterprise policies `WindowManagementAllowedForUrls` and `WindowManagementBlockedForUrls` apply (controlled fixture verifying a URL listed in `WindowManagementBlockedForUrls` throws `NotAllowedError` from `window.setShape()` even when the permission-policy allows it), `Chrome 153` controls (no stable Window Shape API; the feature was Edge 152 OT + Chrome 152 beta OT) report `typeof window.setShape === "undefined"` (the method does not exist on the Chrome 153 baseline), `Safari 26.6` controls (no Window Shape API; Safari has no IWA concept) report `typeof window.setShape === "undefined"`, `Firefox 155` controls (no Window Shape API; Firefox has no IWA concept) report `typeof window.setShape === "undefined"`. Spec reference: the Window Management API spec at `https://wicg.github.io/window-management/` documents the `setShape` extension; the Chrome IWA documentation at `https://chromeos.dev/en/web/isolated-web-apps` documents the IWA + unframed display mode + window-management permission requirements; the sample demo at `https://github.com/paulinagacek/Set-Shape-demo` is a working IWA that demonstrates the API. Acceptance gate: the controlled fixture verifies the live `window.setShape()` round-trip + the `setShape([])` reset + the permission + display-mode gates + the cross-engine parity assertion in a single Playwright session running on Chrome 154 stable on ChromeOS for the live-fire part.
